verdict: READY TO MERGE - 15 of 15 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: Every new test is behavioral: the API tests drive resolve_scope, plan_rows, write_probes and clear_probes against real git repos, and the command tests run the driver as a subprocess with no mocks.
docstring-dispatch joins MUST_EXIT_ZERO, so a refusal cannot pass the root-separation snapshot by doing nothing, and a dedicated test checks that the probe and its record land under the project.
The failure-path tests check that stdout is empty, that every stderr line starts with `problem: `, and that no probe file was left behind.
test_agent_names_the_prompt_lines takes the prompt-line prefixes from DispatchRow.text() instead of hard-coding them, so the agent prose cannot drift from the printed rows.
Path-sensitive cases (drive colon in `::`, cwd-relative tokens, outside-project paths, recursive git-tracked expansion) carry the cross_os mark.

resolve_scope collects every defect (outside root, missing path, non-.py, whole-and-narrowed, ambiguous bare symbols, folder/function name clash, unparseable files) into one DispatchError, so a single run reports the full list instead of failing on the first.

clear_probes deletes only what it can prove is a probe: the path is in the record, carries PROBE_NAME, sits under the project root, is a file and is untracked by git. A corrupted or hand-edited record cannot delete arbitrary files.

write_probes checks every target folder for a tracked file of the probe's name before it writes anything, and records each probe right after writing it, so a later run can always clean up a written probe.
_Parser.error maps argparse failures onto DispatchError, and parse_intermixed_args lets flags sit between paths as the usage text says.
FileScope and DispatchRow forbid extra keys and require a non-empty scope list, so a malformed row fails at construction instead of reaching an agent prompt.
'git ls-files -z' with explicit utf-8 decoding avoids core.quotePath escaping and locale decoding problems for non-ASCII paths on Windows.

The archived spec is a byte-identical move: base blob and docs/plans/strap/_archive/writing-docstrings-187/SkillSpec.json are both 588edc6, so the old frozen proof stays readable unchanged.

important.name: Edit spec base points at a commit outside the branch history
important.summary: The fresh edit SkillSpec records "base": "7009a6e60960f2654aef1edc5a83de8ea30029f7". That commit is the TASK-3 commit from before a rewrite: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 7009a6e 1ea57df` fails, its tree (97d1236) differs from the TASK-3 commit on the branch (0421c4a, tree 1ad5bc5), and it will not exist on the remote after the push, nor locally once gc prunes it. strap.py reads spec.base for an edit baseline (`git show {spec.base}:{part.path}`, strap.py:599) and for the red start commit (strap.py:384). When the show fails, `_skill_text` returns None without an error, so any later baseline on this spec (after an unfreeze, or a new behavior) would run with no SKILL.md, not the base one. The recorded baselines R-1..R-4 can no longer be traced to the base they claim.
fix: Re-open the edit spec through the driver with a base on the branch (0421c4a79c1308c5222daf45821303c7840b31c5 or the merge base 9a65868; SKILL.md, docstring_format.md, docstring_tiers.py and the contract test are byte-identical there to 7009a6e) and refreeze, so base resolves wherever the repo is cloned.
Keep 7009a6e reachable with a pushed ref (for example a tag such as strap/writing-docstrings-0004-base) and say so in the TASK-4 evidence, so the recorded base stays resolvable.

important.name: --clear-probe in SKILL.md anchors at the session cwd, not the probed project
important.summary:
The driver finds the project from --repo, else the first path, else cwd (docstring_dispatch.py:59-68). A run with paths picks the first path's checkout (plan D13 chose that so a d-w worktree file works from the main session), writes its probes there and records them under that checkout's state_dir. The cleanup command in SKILL.md step 2 is bare `docstring_dispatch.py --clear-probe`: no tokens, no --repo. So it resolves the session's cwd checkout, reads that checkout's probes.txt, finds nothing and exits 0. The probes then stay in the worktree's source folders as untracked .py files while the work rows run, waiting for a `git add -A`. D13's own use case leaves the probes behind, and `cleared` printing nothing looks the same as success.

Also (docs): SKILL.md:13 says the guidance "rides on every dispatch prompt as the last line". Step 3 (lines 70-71) adds it only to work-row prompts, and step 2 (line 55) and the agent's Probe row section (docstring-writer.md:165) identify the probe by a row "ending in `Probe: yes`". A session that follows line 13 on the probe row puts `Developer guidance:` after `Probe: yes`, so the probe row no longer ends in that line.

Also (roast): SKILL.md:13 says the guidance 'rides on every dispatch prompt as the last line'. Step 3 (lines 70-71) appends it only to the work rows, and step 2 says nothing either way. The agent recognizes a probe as 'A row ending in `Probe: yes`' (docstring-writer.md:165), and DispatchRow.text puts Probe: yes last. If the session follows line 13 literally, the probe prompt no longer ends in Probe: yes, and the two-line probe reply depends on the agent reading generously.
fix: In SKILL.md step 2, pass the probed project: `... docstring_dispatch.py --clear-probe --repo "<the probe row's Project root>"`, and say the root comes from the probe row's `Project root:` line.
Or have the driver print the exact cleanup command, with --repo filled in, after the probe row (for example on stderr) and have SKILL.md run the printed command.
In SKILL.md:13, replace "rides on every dispatch prompt as the last line" with "rides on every work-row prompt as the last line; the probe row goes out as printed".
SKILL.md:13: change 'rides on every dispatch prompt' to 'rides on every work-row prompt' and add to step 2 that the probe row is dispatched without guidance.
Or docstring-writer.md:165: say 'A row with a `Probe: yes` line' instead of 'A row ending in'.

minor.name: Probe reply says exactly two lines, then allows more on BLOCKED
minor.summary: docstring-writer.md:166-167 asks for "exactly two lines and nothing else", and lines 174-175 say a BLOCKED line is "followed by the refused command or path" without saying where that goes. If the agent puts the command on a line of its own, the reply has more than the two lines SKILL.md:56 tells the session to expect.
fix: In docstring-writer.md:174-175, change "followed by the refused command or path" to "with the refused command or path after it on the same line (`Probe edit: BLOCKED <path>`)".

minor.name: _git skips the project's git-call safeguards
minor.summary:
writing_docstrings_api._git (lines 334-337) runs git with the inherited stdin and no timeout. harness_lib.project.run_git exists to close stdin and bound the wait, and its docstring explains that a child that inherits stdin or never returns stalls the caller. The dispatch driver runs from a skill through the Bash tool, so the same stall can happen there. The utf-8 decoding _git adds is deliberate for 'ls-files -z' output on Windows, so swapping in run_git as it stands would lose it.

Also (roast): The `_git` docstring says it 'Runs git in ``root`` without raising'. subprocess.run raises FileNotFoundError when git is not on PATH, and unlike project.py's git helper it has no timeout. write_probes can also raise OSError (read-only folder, mkdir of the record parent). main() catches only DispatchError and ConfigError (docstring_dispatch.py:94), so any of these prints a traceback. The module docstring (lines 14-15) promises one `problem:` line and exit 1. A failure midway through write_probes also leaves the probes written so far, though they are recorded, so the next run cleans them.
fix: Add stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL and a timeout (reuse project._GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, or a local constant) to the subprocess.run call in _git, and keep encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'.
Give project.run_git an optional encoding argument and call it from _git.

Catch OSError (and subprocess.TimeoutExpired) in docstring_dispatch.main and print it as a `problem:` line with exit 1. In `_git`, add a timeout and turn FileNotFoundError and TimeoutExpired into a failed CompletedProcess, or reword its docstring to say what it actually guarantees.

minor.name: Folder token reports 'no git-tracked .py files' when git itself fails
minor.summary: _tracked_python (lines 386-391) never checks done.returncode. When 'git ls-files' fails (the project root is not a git repository because project_root fell back to CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or the start folder, or git refuses the repo over safe.directory ownership), stdout is empty and _token_files reports '<token>: no git-tracked .py files under it' (line 407). That message is wrong and drops git's stderr, so the developer goes looking for missing files instead of a git problem.
fix: In _tracked_python, return the failure to the caller when done.returncode != 0 (for example, raise or append a problem '<token>: git ls-files failed: <stderr first line>'), and keep the 'no git-tracked .py files' message for a successful empty listing.

minor.name: One mistyped path also reports a 'bare symbols need exactly one file' problem
minor.summary: _merge checks `symbols and len(scopes) != 1` even when the scopes are empty only because the single path failed. `src/zzz.py f` reports 'no such file or directory' plus 'bare symbols f need exactly one file in scope; write <file>::<name>'. The second line sends the developer to rewrite a symbol that was fine. The tests never pair a failing path with a bare symbol, so it passes.
fix: In _merge, skip the bare-symbol count check when `not scopes and problems`, so only the path defect is reported. Add a test that `src/zzz.py f` yields one problem.

minor.name: write_probes clobbers an untracked file of the probe name that no run recorded
minor.summary: In the driver, clear_probes runs first, so every recorded stale probe is already gone when write_probes runs (docstring_dispatch.py:76,85). Any `_docstring_probe.py` still in a target folder therefore belongs to the developer. write_probes overwrites it 'over any untracked stale probe', records it, and the next clear deletes it. --clear-probe is careful to leave unrecorded files alone (test_clear_probe_leaves_an_unrecorded_probe_named_file), and the -p path throws that care away. The name is unlikely to collide, but the result is silent data loss.
fix: In write_probes, refuse an existing untracked probe file the same way it refuses a tracked one ('a file named _docstring_probe.py exists here; remove it or run without -p'). Update test_probes_go_beside_each_folder_over_a_stale_one to clear the record first, or to expect the refusal.

minor.name: OS-level failures escape the one-problem-line contract
minor.summary: The driver docstring promises that every defect is one 'problem:' line on stderr with exit 1, nothing on stdout and no probe written, but main() catches only DispatchError and ConfigError. Several reachable failures bypass that and end in a traceback: probe.write_text in write_probes (read-only target folder) raises OSError after earlier probes in the loop were already written and recorded; path.unlink() in clear_probes (a file locked on Windows) raises OSError and leaves the record in place; _git raises FileNotFoundError when git is not on PATH, which contradicts its own 'without raising' docstring; and a tracked .py symlink that resolves outside the root passes _tracked_python, so _rel's relative_to raises a bare ValueError in _check_names.
fix: Catch OSError in main() next to DispatchError/ConfigError and print it as one 'problem:' line with exit 1; in write_probes, write every probe inside a try that removes the probes already written and re-raises as DispatchError; in _tracked_python, drop resolved paths that fall outside root (or skip them with _inside); reword the _git docstring to 'without raising on a non-zero exit'.
Narrow the driver docstring to defects in the request and state that I/O failures propagate.

minor.name: --clear-probe silently ignores path tokens
minor.summary: The usage line shows '--clear-probe' as a mode on its own, but _output (lines 76-78) returns right after clearing when the flag is set, even when path tokens or --parallel/--include-new were passed. A call like 'docstring_dispatch.py --clear-probe pkg/' exits 0, prints the cleared probes and plans no rows, with nothing to say the request was dropped.
fix: In _output, raise DispatchError(['--clear-probe takes no paths']) when args.clear_probe and args.tokens are both set, before clear_probes runs.

minor.name: Dispatch API module docstring overstates what every test does
minor.summary: The module docstring (lines 3-4) says each test builds a make_project repo and calls writing_docstrings_api directly. test_dispatch_models_forbid_extra_keys (lines 288-298) builds no project and calls only the pydantic models.
fix: Reword to: `Each test but the model check builds a make_project repo and calls writing_docstrings_api directly; the last test validates the row models alone.`

minor.name: Tracked-probe refusal test does not check the record stayed unwritten
minor.summary: write_probes documents that it raises `before writing anything` (writing_docstrings_api.py:512). test_probe_beside_a_tracked_file_of_that_name_is_refused checks only the tracked file's content, not the absence of the probes.txt record, so a version that appended to the record before the tracked check would pass.
fix: Append `assert not _record(root).exists()` after the content assertion.

minor.name: Tracked-file guard of clear_probes is untested
minor.summary: clear_probes skips a recorded probe-named path that git tracks (`or _tracked(root, path)`, writing_docstrings_api.py:542-543), and its docstring promises that. test_clear_probes_removes_only_recorded_probes_under_the_project covers the outside-root and wrong-name branches only; nothing records a tracked _docstring_probe.py, so removing the `_tracked` check would delete a committed file and no test would fail.
fix: Add an API test: make_project with a tracked `src/_docstring_probe.py` holding `kept = 1`, append its POSIX path to the record, assert clear_probes(root, record) == [], the file still reads `kept = 1\n`, and the record is gone.

minor.name: --repo flag and the ConfigError path have no command test
minor.summary: The driver documents `--repo DIR` (docstring_dispatch.py:3,5,14) and _start returns it ahead of the first path (lines 61-62); main also maps ConfigError to a `problem:` line (lines 94-97). No test in the dispatch command suite passes --repo or feeds an invalid .claude/harness.json, so either branch can regress silently.
fix: Add a test that runs from root.parent with `--repo str(root)` and an absolute token and asserts `Project root: <root>`; add one that writes an invalid harness.json in a make_project repo and asserts exit 1 with a `problem: ` line and empty stdout.

minor.name: Unrecorded-probe test never reaches the record filter
minor.summary: test_clear_probe_leaves_an_unrecorded_probe_named_file runs --clear-probe in a project with no probes.txt, so clear_probes returns at its `if not record.is_file(): return []` guard (writing_docstrings_api.py:537-538). The record-driven filter (only recorded paths are removed) is never exercised against a probe-named file that sits outside the record. A clear_probes that, once a record exists, deleted every _docstring_probe.py under the recorded folders or the project would still pass.
fix: Create a record first: run `-p src/a.py src/b.py` (records src/_docstring_probe.py), then write `mine = 1` to pkg/_docstring_probe.py, run --clear-probe, and assert the src probe is gone while pkg/_docstring_probe.py still reads `mine = 1\n`.

minor.name: Contract test pins dispatch flags its docstring says are never copied
minor.summary: The module docstring (lines 4-5) says flags and prompt lines are imported from writing_docstrings_models and never copied, because a pinned literal drifts. test_body_names_every_dispatch_flag hard-codes the driver's flags (line 64) and omits `--repo`, which the parser defines (docstring_dispatch.py:49), and REPLY_HEADINGS / PROBE_LINES (lines 28-30) are copied literals as well. A flag added to or renamed in the parser would not make this test fail.
fix: Load the driver with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location and derive the long and short option strings from `_parser()._actions`, asserting each appears in the SKILL.md body.

Or narrow the docstring to say that the dispatch flags, reply headings and probe lines are pinned on purpose because the agent prose owns them, and add `--repo` to the list or document why it is excluded.
